title: Tencent Tells Investors Its $5 Billion Bond Mainly for AI Capex
source_used: Bloomberg text as carried by The Edge Malaysia; Bloomberg page returns HTTP 403
key_facts: Tencent told fixed-income investors on Monday 12 Oct 2026 that its planned bond offering of about US$5 billion will help finance AI-related capital expenditure, people familiar said.
It could price the deal as early as Tuesday; the offering includes US$1.5 billion to US$2 billion across dollar tranches and 20 billion to 25 billion yuan of offshore yuan notes.
Proceeds are mainly for general corporate purposes such as AI-related capital spending, with the bulk of that spending directed toward chip purchases.
Tencent said it currently has no plans to issue shares or convertible bonds.
Tencent raised capital expenditure by 176% on AI projects and computing to 52.8 billion yuan in the June quarter, causing a free-cash outflow of 13.8 billion yuan.
Its spending is likely to stay elevated through the rest of 2026 and into 2027, at slightly more than 200 billion yuan a year on second-quarter levels, the people said.
Context: SoftBank raised US$11.1 billion in one of the largest junk-bond offerings on record and Alibaba raised a record US$10.2 billion in a follow-on offering.
quote_evidence: Tencent Holdings Ltd told fixed-income investors Monday that its planned bond offering of about US$5 billion (RM20.4 billion) will help finance AI-related capital expenditures, people familiar with the matter said, as it doubles down on the sector.
Tencent said in the investor call that it currently has no plans to issue shares or convertible bonds, added the people, citing the company.
The company hiked capital expenditures by 176% on AI projects and computing to 52.8 billion yuan in the June quarter, triggering a free-cash outflow of 13.8 billion yuan.
why_it_matters_hint: A leading Chinese tech group is borrowing about $5 billion mainly to buy chips for AI.
